newsitem.title: UK: Traditional values endure with Asia's young adults.
newsitem.headline: Traditional values endure with Asia's young adults.

text.p: Asia's 20-something generation is following a distinctive path, blending traditional Asian values with aspects of Western lifestyles, Ogilvy & Mather said in a study on Wednesday.

Ogilvy & Mather Asia/Pacific, part of London-based advertising and marketing holding company WPP Group Plc, said its study showed that the new generation of 20- to 30-year-old Asian adults differs from stereotypes.

"It's been easy to assume that superficial adoption of Western fashions means a deeper influence of the West, and this study suggests this is not the case," Miles Young, president of O&M Asia/Pacific, said in a statement.

Ogilvy & Mather, which conducted 7,000 individual interviews and 66 focus groups across nine markets in across Asia, dubbed the Asian 20-something generation "Genies": the Generation who Independently Engage in Society.
"The Genie differ enormously from their Western counterparts," Mark Blair, regional planning director for O&M Asia/Pacific, said in the study "Uncorking the Genie".
Asian values -- such as hard work, humility, thrift and respect for the family -- endure and there is little sense of crass materialism and moral decline among the Genie group, O&M said.

Looking at the generation from an advertising and marketing viewpoint, O&M noted that Genies do enjoy humourous ads, but that advertising in Asia does not have the same social context it does in the West.
